canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both reviewer blockers remain supported by current code and epic evidence. Reviewer 1's over-large tool-result recovery blocker is confirmed because intake/queued handling applies the large-tier truncation rule, while turn-close recovery independently calls summarizeToolResult without the tier gate or summary parameters. Reviewer 2's absent-derivation fallback logging blocker is confirmed because compose records a dependency gap for missing rows but only emits a recovery receipt when a row exists, and derive logs only recovery receipts. The duplicate rename findings are merged as one nonblocking finding. Gates were rerun locally and passed, with real-inference tests skipped because LHC_OPENROUTER_KEY is unset.
crossStoryFindings: Flows 2 and 3 diverge at consumption-time recovery: the queued tool-result path satisfies over-large tool_result_summary derivations by deterministic truncation, but turn-close recovery reimplements tool-result recovery and can invoke inference for the same tier.
Flow 3 and Flow 5 diverge for absent derivation rows: composition marks a fallback/gap, but the logging path only logs recoveries for existing rows.
No material fake adapter, hidden shim, placeholder provider, or non-real default production path was verified under packages/lhc/src; deterministic providers remain explicit test/config fixtures.
architectureFindings: Tech-design DD-3 requires tool results above the large tier to land ready by deterministic truncation with no inference item/provider call; packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/index.ts:150-196 and packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/handlers.ts:145-159 implement that for intake/queued work, but packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:117-127 bypasses it during recovery.

Tech-design DD-5 and epic AC-3.6/AC-5.3 require fallback events to be logged separately from derivation state; packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/compose.ts:222-238 omits a RecoveryReceipt when the derivation row is absent, so packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:196-211 has nothing to log.

The form-to-derivation rename is incomplete at the production vocabulary level: schema/shared types are renamed, but production modules still expose form-named files, helpers, constants, and comments.
epicCoverageAssessment: Story Gate passed locally: cd packages/lhc && pnpm run verify completed with 47 test files passed, 426 tests passed, and 9 skipped.
Epic Gate passed locally: cd packages/lhc && pnpm run verify-all completed with 47 test files passed, 426 tests passed, and 9 skipped.

Coverage remains incomplete for cross-story recovery: tests cover over-large tool results on intake/queued handling and normal composition fallback, but not failed/pending over-large tool_result_summary recovery at turn close.
Coverage remains incomplete for absent derivation-row fallback logging: tests cover pending/failed row fallback logging, but not missing-row fallback logging.
Flow 5/6 logging and runtime-change coverage is otherwise present; Flow 0 rename coverage is partial because stale production vocabulary remains.
productionPathFindings: packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:117-127 performs a real provider call for tool_result_summary recovery with raw content, unknown_tool, no targetTokens, and no guidance. For over-large tool results this violates the deterministic truncation/no-inference production invariant.

packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/compose.ts:148-153 correctly defines the tool-result fallback as truncateForFallback, but recoverMessageForms runs before composition and can replace a non-ready row with provider output, preventing the deterministic floor path from being used for over-large sources.
Smart compact was not found to call a provider in the inspected production path; compact resolves chunk material through the turns surface and stored-member concatenation.

blockingFindings.title: Turn-close recovery bypasses the tool-result large-tier gate
blockingFindings.evidence: The queued handler returns truncateForFallback(content) as ready with no provider call when estimateTokens(content) exceeds largeTierTokens at packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/handlers.ts:145-159; intake also writes the large summary ready and avoids queueing at packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/index.ts:150-196. Turn-close recovery separately calls run.provider.summarizeToolResult for tool_result_summary at packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:117-127 with raw content, toolName unknown_tool, no targetTokens, and no guidance. This violates AC-2.3, AC-2.7, AC-3.3, and DD-3 for over-large tool results.

blockingFindings.title: Absent derivation fallback is not logged
blockingFindings.evidence: packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/compose.ts:222-238 creates a DependencyGap whenever a derivable component falls back, but creates a RecoveryReceipt only when form !== undefined. packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:196-211 logs only recoveries. Therefore an absent smoothed_prompt or tool_result_summary row can render through fallback and record a gap without producing the fallback log entry required by AC-3.6 and AC-5.3.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Form-to-derivation rename remains incomplete in production vocabulary
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The epic scope and DD-1 require a total form-to-derivation rename. blockingFindings.title: Turn-close recovery bypasses tool-result tier gate and can call the provider on over-large tool results
blockingFindings.evidence: The queued handler gates tool results with estimateTokens(content) > largeTierTokens and returns truncateForFallback(content) ready with no provider call in packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/handlers.ts:145-159; intake even avoids queueing such work in packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/index.ts:150-196. The turn-close recovery path independently calls run.provider.summarizeToolResult with raw content at packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:117-127, with no token check, no targetTokens, no paired tool name, and no guidance. That violates AC-2.3/AC-2.7 and the production-path invariant that large tool results truncate rather than inference-summarize.
